beats.story: The morning has just settled after the chaos hour of people marching around to caffeinate, put lunch bullshit in the fridge, and pretend to care about Marsha's opinion of the TV show she watched last night with her husband. Armin slipped in about fifteen minutes late, with bloodshot eyes and a pale forehead, all recorded by Rhonda. I take a long swig of coffee and swish it around in my mouth to warm my tongue, still cottony from the wine last night. I tried not to, but it was the meeting with Cliff. Every time I closed my eyes on the bus home, I saw her. Specifically, her face when she realized my lie . . .
beats.story_cn: 晨间混乱方才平息——咖啡因朝圣者们已巡游完毕，午餐饭盒塞进了冰箱，也假装关心了玛莎对昨晚夫妻剧集的高见。阿尔明踩着迟到十五分钟的节点溜进来时，眼白爬满血丝，额发湿漉漉贴在惨白额头上，这一切都被朗达记录在案。我猛灌一大口咖啡，任苦涩液体在口腔里滚过一圈暖热舌尖，昨夜红酒留下的棉絮感还未散尽。我试过不去想的，可那是和克里夫的会面啊。每当在公交车上阖眼，她的脸就会浮现——确切地说，是她识破我谎言时那张脸…

beats.story: I need to focus. Today is a new day. Today will be better. When I passed Caitlin's desk this morning on the way to my own, I saw she had several documents open; she's probably working on ideas for the multi-unit meeting. I should be doing the same, but this particular battle might already be lost. Coming up with ideas is the easy part. It's the speaking-in-front-of-the-group piece -- all their beady eyes and dry expressions zooming in on me -- that always sends me into a panic and trips me up. I'm just going to have to beat the system from the side.
beats.story_cn: 我必须集中精神。今天是崭新的一天，今天会更好。今早经过凯特琳工位时，我瞥见她屏幕摊开着好几份文档——八成在为多部门联席会攒点子。我本该做同样的事，但这场战役或许早已输在起跑线。想点子从来不是难事。真正令我窒息的是站在聚光灯下开口陈述——那些小眼珠与漠然表情齐刷刷聚焦过来的时刻，总让我溃败失语。这次我得从侧面迂回击破系统。

beats.story: As if on cue, a DM dings onto my screen from Caitlin to Rhonda, and I am all too eager to read it. Hey, remember to send me the May inventory data today and then Jolene tomorrow? Understanding dawns on me. No wonder Caitlin's been so fast lately! "Can you give me the leg up again this month?" Caitlin had asked Rhonda yesterday. I couldn't figure out how she was managing to complete her spreadsheet only an hour after the data arrived, but holy shit, Rhonda's been giving her a sneak peek. What a sad, petty little place this is. At least I have a leg up of my own this round.
beats.story_cn: 仿佛算准时机，屏幕上叮咚弹出凯特琳发给朗达的私信，我简直贪婪地逐字吞咽：“记得今天先发我五月库存数据，明天再发乔琳！”霎时间我全明白了。难怪凯特琳最近效率高得反常！“这个月能再给我开次小灶吗？”她昨天这样问朗达时，我还琢磨不透她怎么能在数据送达一小时内填完表格。天啊，原来朗达一直在给她开绿色通道。这地方真够可悲又狭隘。至少这回，我手里也有了自己的底牌。

He hasn't even sent it on to Rhonda yet! Caitlin's responsible for A to M in this grid, and I, L to Z. It's going to be glorious when I complete mine first, even with no "advantage." I just can't believe they've stooped to this flat-out method of sabotage. And Caitlin was so brazen about asking; clearly, they've been doing this for a while. If they're keeping the monthly inventory grids from me, what else could they be hiding? I click into Rhonda's inbox. And holy hell, it's awful here.
beats.story_cn: 我切进格雷戈里的邮箱——这次带着十二分警惕，毕竟还没做好直面人性阴暗面的心理准备。果然，所有分部数据昨晚就已抵达，他甚至还没转发给朗达！凯特琳负责表格A至M区，我负责L至Z区。若我能在毫无“优势”的情况下率先完成，那场面该多痛快。只是没想到他们竟堕落到用如此赤裸裸的手段使绊子。凯特琳索要资料时竟毫无愧色，显然这种勾当已成惯例。如果他们连月度库存表都要瞒我，还能藏着什么？我点进朗达的收件箱。老天，这里的场面更不堪入目。

beats.story: It's a sea of red flags marking emails as "to-do," but aside from that, there's barely any organization whatsoever. It's appalling how much vital information she has access to that she hasn't shared. There is one subfolder with a curious title: Things to Figure Out. I click it open. Every email is from Gregory. A whole collection of requests, some dating back months. And she hasn't done them. He asked her to digitize several archives and to create online versions of common documents.
beats.story_cn: 那简直是一片标着“待办”的邮件全都标红的海洋，像一片刺眼的红旗海，但除此之外，几乎谈不上任何条理。最令人咋舌的是，她手头掌握着这么多关键信息，却一条都未曾分享。有个子文件夹标题很奇怪：“待弄清之事”。我点开它。每封邮件都来自格雷戈里。满满一盒子请求，有些甚至积压了好几个月。而她一件都没办。他让她把若干档案数字化，并为常用文件创建在线版本。

beats.story: She's replied to him, On it :), but I can't find any evidence that she's touched a thing. I peer over my cubicle wall. She's filling out a hard copy of the EAE schedule with a pencil as she munches on an apple. "Drat," she says, as she picks up the only physical eraser in the office. Back in her inbox, I see last month's corporate credit card statement has come through for the card she reported missing. I have to stifle a giggle. Whoever stole Miss Rhonda Staples's company card somehow managed to charge $64.12 to the Supershops Liquor Depot the day before the account was closed. Bold of them to use it where you can get a company discount.
beats.story_cn: 她回复他说：“马上处理 :)”，但我找不到任何证据表明她碰过那堆东西。我探头越过隔板墙，看到她正一边啃着苹果，一边用铅笔填写EAE计划表的纸质版。“哎呀，”她嘟囔着，拿起了办公室里唯一一个实体橡皮擦。再看她的收件箱，我发现了上个月的公司信用卡账单——正是她申报丢失的那张卡。我差点没憋住笑。不知是哪位“好汉”，竟在账户被冻结的前一天，用罗达·斯坦普尔斯小姐的公司卡在“超级商店酒水批发”刷了64.12美元。胆子真不小，还敢在能享受公司折扣的地方用。

beats.story: No wonder HQ flagged it as suspicious. Did Rhonda accidentally charge a personal expense and then report it stolen? Maybe that's why she seemed a bit cagey when Gregory asked. Beneath her emails is a folder that contains her desk phone's log records. She's on that thing all day long, so I quickly skim through it. Mostly she's talking to other department heads or to Gregory. But one odd pattern draws the eye. Every day, like clockwork, she calls the same outside number at least four times.
beats.story_cn: 怪不得总部将其标记为可疑。难道是罗达不小心把私人消费记在了卡上，然后才谎称丢失？也许这就是为什么格雷戈里询问时，她显得有点闪烁其词。在她邮件下方，有个文件夹存放着她办公座机的通话记录。她一天到晚占着那条线，我迅速浏览了一遍。大多是在和其他部门主管或格雷戈里通话。但一个奇怪的规律吸引了我的目光：每天，像上了闹钟一样，她至少往同一个外部号码打四次电话。

beats.story: And every single time, it's marked as unanswered. I scroll back at least seven months and it seems almost ritualistic -- like she's calling a ghost. It's probably nothing, but I pull a Post-it from my drawer and write the number down. I shift to Caitlin's inbox next. Unlike Rhonda, she's got folders for everything. And subfolders inside of those folders. I start to wonder if she makes a new folder for every piece of mail she receives. Then I come across one with the title Passwords.
beats.story_cn: 而且每一次，通话记录都显示“未接通”。我往回翻了至少七个月，这几乎成了一种仪式——就像她在给一个幽灵打电话。可能没什么，但我还是从抽屉里撕下一张便利贴，记下了那个号码。接着，我转向凯特琳的收件箱。和罗达不同，她为每类东西都建了文件夹，文件夹里还有子文件夹。我开始怀疑，她是不是每收一封邮件就新建一个文件夹。然后，我看到了一个标题为“密码”的文件夹。

beats.story: I open that bitch up so fast -- and ding ding ding! It's a freaking folder full of her passwords for work. She emails them to her personal box monthly. Her most recent one from April 13 reads: Work email and login: Iamworthy44 Inventory spreadsheet: Iambeautiful19* Work folder: Iamagoddess19* Please let me hold it together. Let my cackling at her expense stay inside my heart. My mouth twitches, threatening a chuckle. She's actually typing this stuff to herself several times a day? No wonder she's so cocky.
beats.story_cn: 我飞快地撬开了那贱人的邮箱——叮叮叮！里面居然有个文件夹，装满了她所有的工作密码。她每月都把这些密码发到私人邮箱。最近一封来自4月13日，上面写着：工作邮箱和登录名：Iamworthy44，库存表密码：Iambeautiful19*，工作文件夹密码：Iamagoddess19*。老天，请让我稳住。请让这份幸灾乐祸的窃笑只留在心底。我的嘴角抽动着，差点笑出声。她一天竟然把这种东西给自己发好几遍？怪不得她那么嚣张。

beats.story: Then my excitement withers; obviously I can't use her passwords to actually send anything. She would definitely notice that, and the goal is to not get fired. But now I can at least log in to her locked folders. I quickly add the passwords to the Post-it note, while glancing from side to side to make sure no one sees. Not all spies get the glamour of one Jean Adler heavy breathing outside Gregory's office while wiping dandruff from his glasses. "Hello again, everyone." I nearly vault out of my seat from shock, half shoving the Post-it under my keyboard. Cliff is striding around the corner with a familiar yellow box in his hands. He's wearing a blue plaid shirt that looks really soft.
beats.story_cn: 紧接着我的兴奋劲儿就消退了；显然，我不能用她的密码真的去发什么东西。她肯定会注意到，而目标是保住饭碗。但至少现在我能登录她那些加密的文件夹了。我飞速把密码抄在便利贴上，同时左右张望，确保没人看见。不是每个间谍都能像让·阿德勒那样，隔着格雷戈里的办公室门都能上演一段呼吸急促擦眼镜的戏码。“各位，又见面了。”我差点从座位上弹起来，慌忙把便利贴塞到键盘底下。克莱夫正大步转过拐角，手里拿着个熟悉的黄色盒子。他穿着一件看起来非常柔软的蓝格子衬衫。

beats.story: "I'm going to be booking meetings with each of you over the next week. I just want to get to know more about you and your roles here. It's really an open mic for you to share anything." At the blank stares, he clears his throat. "So, just wanted to come by again, so you know the meeting request isn't spam or anything bad." He points to himself. "I'm a real guy on the fourth floor and my door is always open." Expressionless sets of eyeballs, including my own, peer at him like emojis. "And these donuts are real too," he adds. His chuckle mixes with the sound of keyboards frantically typing -- and so the gossip mill begins. I feel pain in an unknown part of my body on his behalf.
beats.story_cn: “接下来一周我会约各位单独开会，只想更了解大家和各位的工作范畴。这纯粹是开放平台，让你们畅所欲言。”见众人一脸茫然，他清了清嗓子，“所以特意再来一趟，免得大家以为会议邀约是垃圾邮件或别的什么。”他指指自己，“我是四楼的真实存在的活人，办公室大门永远敞开。”一双双包括我在内的无表情眼球，像表情符号般盯着他。“这些甜甜圈也是真的，”他补充道。轻笑声与噼里啪啦的键盘声交织——八卦流水线正式启动。我替他感到某处未知器官隐隐作痛

beats.story: But then Cliff locks eyes with me and his expression brightens. "Jolene, hey!" All my pity for him vanishes in an instant. I catch Caitlin smirking, and she shifts her gaze from Cliff to me. My skin tightens as more eyes tilt in my direction. I give Cliff a small, curt nod. I can't even muster a smile. He doesn't seem to register the vibes I'm giving off, because he makes his way to my desk and leans an arm against my cubicle wall. The sweet scent that permeated his office has followed him here, and everything in me seems to liquefy.
beats.story_cn: 但克里夫与我四目相对时，神色骤然明朗。“乔琳，嘿！”我对他的那点怜悯瞬间蒸发。瞥见凯特琳嘴角的讥笑，她将目光从克里夫转向我。更多视线聚焦过来，我的皮肤绷紧了。我只对他短促微点下头，连微笑都挤不出。他似乎完全没察觉我释放的疏离信号，径直走到我桌前，手肘支在我隔间墙壁上。那弥漫他办公室的甜香随之飘来，我体内所有器官仿佛瞬间液化

Cliff should know that you don't give the fucking vultures anything while you're in the ring. At best, he's reminded everyone that we know each other because of my mandatory training. But at worst . . . The last thing I need is my fellow professionals picturing me having sex, which is a thing people do when they think two people are dating.

beats.story: Then he leans over a touch more into my cube's space and points a finger toward my desk. "Hey, can I have that Post-it?" My stomach nearly drops onto the carpet. My head whips toward my keyboard, where the incriminating yellow paper I'd shoved under it is poking out. Then I realize Cliff's finger is actually pointing at the block of unused notes. I shove the whole thing toward him, too relieved to trust myself to speak. He takes a piece from the top as well as the pen that had nearly rolled off the corner of my desk and holds them up to my cube wall so he can scribble a quick note. "Well, it was nice to see you all," he announces to the room. "I'll go back to my cave now." He holds his head high, but his shoulders have a slump to them as he walks over to the donut box and presses the note on top of it.
beats.story_cn: 接着，他身子往前探了探，几乎要探进我的格子间，手指朝我的桌子一点。“嘿，能给我张便利贴吗？”我的胃猛地往下一沉。脑袋“唰”地转向键盘——那张惹祸的黄色纸片，正从我慌忙塞进去的键盘底下探出头来。随即我才意识到，克里夫的手指其实是指向那整叠没用过的便签纸。我把那叠纸整个推给他，如释重负得连话都说不利索。他抽出最上面一张，又拿起差点滚下桌角的笔，靠在我的格子间隔板上快速写了张便条。“好了，很高兴见到大家，”他朝整个办公室宣布，“我这就回我的洞穴了。”他昂着头，但走过去把便条按在甜甜圈盒子上时，肩膀却垮了下来。

beats.story: More crickets as he disappears down the hallway, the blue jeans schedule sheet on the bulletin board flapping in his wake. A split second after he's cleared the room, it's like someone's hit the on button. Chairs push back, footsteps descend upon the box. Rhonda, Armin, and Caitlin are the first to arrive on the scene, pulling the lid back and tearing into the little gourmet treats. Heat burns through my stomach as I watch them pick the box clean like hyenas. Jean Adler scrunches his face so close to the box that I'm sure there's a powdered dandruff flavor being made before our eyes. "These are from that new place," Armin says as he pops one in his mouth. "I'm not saying they're good, but I've just found the will to live." Caitlin places a hand on his shoulder.
beats.story_cn: 他沿着走廊消失后，办公室里又是一片鸦雀无声，只有公告板上那张蓝色牛仔裤排班表在他身后扑簌作响。他前脚刚踏出房间，后脚就像有人按下了启动键。椅子猛地推开，脚步声纷沓而至涌向盒子。朗达、阿明和凯特琳第一个扑到现场，掀开盒盖就开始撕扯那些精致的小点心。看着他们像鬣狗一样把盒子扫荡一空，一股灼热感在我胃里翻腾。吉恩·阿德勒把脸挤得离盒子那么近，我敢说我们亲眼目睹了糖霜头屑味的诞生。“这是新开那家店的，”阿明塞了一个进嘴里说道，“我不是说它有多好，但我刚刚找回了活下去的意志。”凯特琳把手搭在他肩上。

beats.story: "You have to stop pulling all- nighters. You're too old to be gaming like that." He blinks through his puffed eyes. "I wasn't online last night." "Has he booked a meeting with you yet?" Marla asks Caitlin. Caitlin huffs. "Not yet, but I've got plenty to say." The insistent way Caitlin glances at Armin makes acid burn in my stomach. But both their gazes draw to me too quick. I drop my eyes, but not in time. Caitlin makes a big show of taking her hand off Armin's shoulder as she hardens her stare at him.
beats.story_cn: “你别再通宵熬夜了。你这把年纪，不该再这么玩游戏。”他眨着浮肿的眼睛。“我昨晚没在线。”“他约你谈了吗？”玛拉问凯特琳。凯特琳哼了一声。“还没，但我可有一肚子话要说。”凯特琳看向阿明时那执着的眼神，让我胃里直冒酸水。可他们的目光太快也扫向了我。我垂下眼睛，但已经来不及。凯特琳夸张地把手从阿明肩上拿开，同时冷冷地盯住了他。

beats.story: She continues. "What's weird is he's trying to act like he's our friend, when we all know what he's really here for." But they don't know the half of it. I stare, imploding inside, when a message from Cliff appears on my screen. CLIFF: Hey, sorry if I assumed -- no pressure if you don't want to carpool today. I should've confirmed via email. The pit in my stomach hardens as I picture him, typing to me alone from his trinket-filled office after that embarrassing display. He's the only person who's been nice to me for no reason here. And I'm a venti-sized pile of shit.
beats.story_cn: 她继续煽风点火：“蹊跷的是他假装和咱们称兄道弟，可谁不知道他打什么算盘。”但她们连真相的皮毛都没摸到。我僵在原地，内心世界正在坍缩成黑洞时，克里夫的消息突然弹进屏幕。克里夫：嘿，如果我太唐突先道歉——今天不想拼车完全没压力。我本该用邮件确认的。胃部那口深井在我脑补画面时凝成冰块：那个让我出尽洋相的下午，他正独自坐在摆满小摆件的办公室里给我发消息。他是这里唯一毫无理由对我释放善意的人。而我，是个超大杯容量的人渣。

The swarm is beginning to dissipate from the donut box, so I stand up and head over. However, there's nothing left -- these animals have picked it clean. The Post-it Cliff left on top reads: Not Poison ;) I peel it off. I take it back to my desk and stuff it in my locked drawer along with the more incriminating one containing the passwords. Caitlin finishes off the last bite of her second donut and says, "He could've sprung for full-sized ones." Bunch of dickheads.
beats.story_cn: 我和收件箱来回拉扯两回合，发现不回复已成时间洪流中唯一的选择。那群鬣狗正从甜甜圈盒边散开，我起身前往前线——但战场已被洗劫一空。盒顶粘着克里夫的便签：非毒药;)。我揭下那张纸，将它与更罪证确凿的密码纸条一起锁进抽屉。凯特琳咽下第二个甜甜圈的最后一口，评论道：“他好歹该买正常尺寸的。”一群混账。
